full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 05.01.2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No.58 of 2009 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 20.02.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Seventh Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.92 of 2006 decreeing the same. 

 5.  The learned Joint District Judge, Seventh Court, Dhaka by his judgments and order dated 20.02.2008 decreed the suit on contest against defendant Nos.7 and 10 and ex-parte against the remaining defendants Without any order as to costs. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Seventh Court, Dhaka, the Janata Bank Ltd. defendant No.10 preferred First Appeal No. 58 of 2009 and defendant No.7 preferred First Appeal No. 135 of 2008 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division upon hearing both the appeals by the judgment and order dated 05.01.2010 dismissed the appeals. 

 7. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division, the defendant-leave petitioner has preferred this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division. 

 8. Mr. M. Khaled Ahmed, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, submits that defendant No.1 being the owner of the suit land mortgaged it with Janata Bank and that as defendant No.1 failed to pay off the outstanding loan amount, the bank had to file the Certificate Case No.03.JB/87 before the General Certificate Officer, Narayangonj and that the mortgaged property was sold in pursuance of the certificate case and as such, the plaintiff did not have the authority to file the instant suit to challenge the auction sale and the High Court Division without taking into consideration this aspect of the case dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court and as such, impugned judgment should be set aside. He further submits that the plaintiff's suit is barred by section 37 of the Public Demands Recovery Act and as such, the impugned judgment and decree affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court should be set aside.
